- §z$$sound_origin_pos_y §r= The Y position of the sound's origin
- §z$$sound_origin_pos_z §r= The Z position of the sound's origin
- §z$$sound_origin_distance_to_player §r= The distance between the player and the sound origin
- §z$$sound_origin_direction_from_player §r= Direction in degrees (0-360) relative to where the player is facing when the sound started

- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position

languages.English:
Reads text from a local file or remote URL and returns it.
Supports reading entire content or only the last few lines.

Content is cached to improve performance:
- Local files: Re-read every 1 second
- URLs: Re-read every 10 seconds

Required values:
- path_or_url: The file path or URL to read from
  Local files: Use a path inside the active Minecraft instance (e.g. 'config/myfile.txt')
  Remote files: Use HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g. 'https://example.com/data.txt')
  
The file path can start with '.minecraft/' to target the default .minecraft directory. Paths cannot leave either selected root.

Optional values:
- mode: How to read the content (default: 'all')
  Options: 'all' (entire content), 'last' (last X lines)
- separator: Text between lines when joining (default: '\n')
  Common options: '\n' (newline), ' | ', ', ', ' '
- last_lines: Number of lines to return in 'last' mode (default: 1)
  Only used when mode is 'last'

Note: When mode is 'last' with last_lines set to 1,
the single line is returned without any separator.

Returns empty string if source is not cached yet, doesn't exist,
cannot be read, or if there's no internet connection for URLs.

§xSecurity: Imported customizations can use this placeholder to read files inside these roots and combine the result with network actions. Only import customizations you trust, and inspect their placeholders and actions first.

  Remote files: Use HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g. 'https://example.com/data.txt')
  
The file path can start with '.minecraft/' to target the default .minecraft directory. Paths cannot leave either selected root.

- last_lines: Number of lines to return in 'last' mode (default: 1)
  Only used when mode is 'last'

Note: When mode is 'last' with last_lines set to 1,
the single line is returned without any separator.

languages.English:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers whenever an entity dies anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that died
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player to the death position (returns -1 when the entity died in another dimension)
- §z$$death_pos_x §r= The X coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$death_pos_y §r= The Y coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$death_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate where the entity died
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the entity that died
- §z$$dimension_key §r= The dimension the entity died in
- §z$$damage_type §r= The resource location of the damage type that caused the death
- §z$$is_same_dimension_as_player §r= If TRUE, the entity died in the same dimension as the player
- §z$$entity_killed_by_name §r= The plain text name of the killer or NONE when unavailable
- §z$$entity_killed_by_key §r= The resource location of the killer's type (uses minecraft:player for players, NONE when unavailable)
- §z$$entity_killed_by_uuid §r= The UUID of the killer or NONE when unavailable

Toggles villager trading enhancements.

This allows you to bookmark one or more type of trades.
And do all possible trades for these types
with a single click.

There are 2 types of bookmarks Global and Local.
 - Global select the trade type for all villagers with the same profession.
 - Local select the trade for the active villager only.

Bookmarks also work for Wandering Traders but they only have Global type.

languages.English:
This action deletes a file or folder in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

Append '*' to the end of the target path to delete every file directly inside that folder. This wildcard ignores sub-directories and leaves the folder itself intact.

Provide the download folder instead of a file name; FancyMenu derives the saved file name from the HTTP response headers or the URL automatically.

§lAsynchronous Download:§r This action downloads files asynchronously, which means the download happens in the background without freezing or blocking the game. The game will continue running normally while the file is being downloaded.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

languages.English:
Checks if an element is focused in its parent screen.
Some elements get focused when you interact with them, like buttons or sliders.
For buttons and sliders you will then see an outline, like they are hovered, but they can also get focused when using the arrow keys or the Tab key to navigate in screens.

This is useful, because in case of arrow or Tab key navigation, elements will not be seen as 'hovered', so the 'Is Element Hovered' requirement would not return true then.

It is important to note that not every type of element can be focused. Most of the time it's only buttons and sliders.

languages.English:
This listener triggers whenever video playback state changes.

Possible values for §z$$new_status§r:
- PLAYING: Video started and is now playing (including when resuming from pause)
- STOPPED: Video was stopped through stop()
- PAUSED: Video was paused through pause()
- FINISHED: Video naturally reached the end of playback

If looping is enabled, FINISHED is emitted when the end is reached, right before the next loop starts.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$video_source §r= The source of the video (local path, web URL or resource location)
- §z$$video_source_type §r= Source type (LOCAL, WEB, RESOURCE_LOCATION)
- §z$$is_looping §r= TRUE if looping is enabled, otherwise FALSE
- §z$$new_status §r= New playback status (PLAYING, STOPPED, PAUSED, FINISHED)

languages.English:
In offset mode, the target elements will use their
normal position as origin and get animated starting from this
position instead of getting their position completely overridden.

In this mode, keyframes get saved in a different way.
The middle of the screen (crosshair) stands for
the target element and you should record keyframes
around this crosshair.
Keyframes recorded in offset mode are not compatible
with the normal mode an vice-versa, so you should
choose a mode before start recording.

languages.English:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

This listener triggers whenever an entity spawns anywhere on the connected server/world (even if the player is far away or in another dimension).

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the spawned entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player to the spawn location (returns -1 when the entity spawned in another dimension)
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate at spawn time
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the spawned entity
- §z$$dimension_key §r= The dimension the entity spawned in
- §z$$is_same_dimension_as_player §r= If TRUE, the entity spawned in the same dimension as the player

languages.English:
Returns either the current play time of a Video element
(MM:SS format), the play progress percentage (0-100), or the current play time in milliseconds.
Returns '00:00' or '0' if the element is not ready yet or no video is set.

Required values:
- element_identifier: The ID of the Video element
- show_percentage: Set to 'true' to show percentage instead of time
- output_as_timestamp: Set to 'true' to show milliseconds instead of MM:SS

Priority:
- show_percentage (highest)
- output_as_timestamp
- default MM:SS output

languages.English:
Listeners are a very powerful feature that allows you to execute an action script when specific things happen, like when a user types on their keyboard, performs a mouse click or even when things happen in worlds, like when the player dies.

Listeners aren't bound to screens, so they constantly listen for events, even if there isn't a screen open at all, like when playing in a singleplayer world or on a server.

languages.English:
This listener triggers after the 'Select File' action finishes.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$selected_file_path §r= The absolute path of the chosen file (empty when the dialog was cancelled)
- §z$$target_file_path §r= The resolved path inside the Minecraft instance that received the file
- §z$$selection_succeeded §r= 'true' when the file was copied successfully
- §z$$selection_cancelled §r= 'true' when the dialog was closed without selecting a file
- §z$$failure_reason §r= Error information when the action failed

languages.English:
Replaces text in a string using either literal text or regular expressions (regex).
Supports both single replacement and replace-all operations.

Required values:
- text: The input text to perform replacements on
- search: The text or regex pattern to search for

Optional values:
- replacement: The replacement text (default: empty string)
- use_regex: Set to 'true' to use regex patterns (default: 'false')
- replace_all: Set to 'true' to replace all occurrences, otherwise only first occurrence (default: 'true')

When using regex, you can use capture groups like $1, $2, etc.

languages.English:
All versions. Modifies DFU initialization to happen the first time something needs to be upgraded. This sounds similar to LazyDFU but is distinctly implemented, as it avoids loading *any* DFU classes/data structures, while LazyDFU only disables rule optimization. Essentially, this option is a safer version of DataFixerSlayer as it will still load DFU when needed.

You should typically continue to use LazyDFU even with this option enabled, as otherwise DFU rule optimization will cause lag.

Minecraft has run out of memory.

This could be caused by a bug in the game or by the Java Virtual Machine not being allocated enough memory.

To prevent level corruption, the current game has quit. We've tried to free up enough memory to let you go back to the main menu and back to playing, but this may not have worked.

Please restart the game if you see this message again.

Minecraft wear it brave state out of memory.
 
This couldst beest didst cause by an issue in the game 'r by the Java Virtual Machine that it shall never cut from memory.

languages.English: All versions. Many mods ship outdated structure files, which requires the game to upgrade them using DFU every single time they are loaded. This can be quite slow. This patch adds logic to instead save the upgraded version of the structure, and reuse it on the next load. To handle the case that the mod changes a structure file but not the name, the original file's hash is compared against the cached version, and if they do not match the structure will be upgraded again.

languages.English:
1.16 & 1.19 only. **A key optimization.**

In the middle of the 1.16 development cycle, Forge patched the game to reload datapacks twice when loading an existing world, in order to fix an issue with biome ID shifting. Unfortunately, datapack reloads often take upwards of 30 seconds and so this very severely affects world loading times.

ModernFix makes the necessary changes to avoid this reload, based on the unfinished Forge PR #8163.

This change was removed by Forge in 1.18, but then a similar patch was added *again* in 1.19 to fix mod datapacks not being loaded when creating new singleplayer worlds. Fortunately, the issue is localized to the world creation screen in 1.19, and existing worlds only require a single reload. However, this still doubles the length of the lag spike when clicking "Create New World" in 1.19, and so ModernFix again makes changes to not perform a redundant reload.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$source_zip_path §r= The source ZIP file path
- §z$$target_folder_path §r= The target folder path the ZIP was extracted to
- §z$$extract_succeeded §r= If the ZIP extraction was successful (true/false)
- §z$$failure_reason §r= The failure reason if the extraction failed (empty string if successful)

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the entity type that was targeted
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The last measured distance from the player's eyes to the entity hit position
- §z$$entity_pos_x §r= The entity's X coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the entity that was targeted

languages.English:
Select a shader source file from local storage, a web URL, or a resource location.
The file must contain plain text GLSL fragment shader code (not binary).
Accepted entry points:
- Shadertoy style: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
- Direct fragment style: void main()
In direct mode, output should be written to an out vec4 variable (recommended) or gl_FragColor compatibility.
Supported local file extension: .txt only.
Important: extension is only used for filtering; the content must still be fragment shader code.

languages.English:
This action extracts a ZIP file into a folder in the game directory, which starts at the root of the Minecraft instance directory. The target path includes the folder name the ZIP content gets extracted to, and no extra folders get created named like the ZIP file.

This action is limited to work only inside the game directory for safety reasons.

It is also possible to access the default '.minecraft' directory with this action. For that, just start paths with the '.minecraft/' prefix.

This action extracts asynchronously and triggers the 'On ZIP Extracted via Action' listener when finished.

When you enable the template mode for a custom button, it will apply
some of its settings to all other buttons or sliders in the current screen.

Template buttons will be §linvisible§r outside the editor.

When you set the template to share settings with sliders, the
settings for the button textures will change to slider texture settings.

§lSettings that get shared are:

- Button/Slider Textures
- Button Click Sounds
- Button/Slider Hover Sounds
- Button/Slider Position (if enabled)

Hold §6[shift]§r to automatically pick based on your inventory

Right click a recipe node to fold it temporarily
Hold §6[shift]§r to clear the recipe

The initial tree state is controlled by default recipes
A button next to recipes can set default recipe preferences

The toggle by total cost can be used to help craft a recipe tree
While crafting, materials that need to be collected will be displayed
§bSynthetic favorites§r will be added to the favorites sidebar that
will show incomplete steps and can be used to craft

languages.English:
Adds a Delay Gate block. On the first reach, it starts a one-time timer and skips its contained actions. The surrounding script continues immediately.

This block does not schedule an execution. Its timer is checked only when the script reaches the same block instance again. Reaches before the timer expires skip the contained actions. The first reach at or after expiry opens the gate and runs them; every later reach runs them immediately.

Delay time is in milliseconds. A resolved delay of 0 or less, including invalid values, opens the gate immediately.

The gate resets only when that action-script instance is reconstructed or replaced.

Use Execute Later instead when every reach should schedule a fresh delayed execution.

languages.English:
§xRequires FancyMenu on the server.§r

Fetches live NBT data from the server, mirroring every target supported by '/data get'.
Returns an empty value until the server response arrives.

The placeholder works exactly like the '/data get' command, so everything that should be possible with the command should also be possible with the placeholder.

Supported source_type values:
- entity: Full selector syntax (scores, advancements, predicates, rotation, gamemode, etc.)
- block: Absolute, relative (~) or local (^) coordinates like the vanilla command
- storage: Command storage identifiers (namespace:key)

Optional arguments:
- nbt_path: Same path rules as '/data get'
- scale: Multiplies numeric results (default 1.0)
- return_type: 'value', 'string', 'snbt', or 'json'

Responses are cached for 100ms to avoid spamming the server.

languages.English:
Picks a random line from a TXT file, URL or direct plain text.

Supports local files, remote URLs and plain text as "source":
- Local files: Use relative paths (e.g. '/config/fancymenu/assets/tips.txt')
- Remote files: Use HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g. 'https://example.com/tips.txt')
- Plain text: Input direct plain text. Separate lines with "\n".

Content is automatically reloaded every 30 seconds to pick up changes.

The 'interval' parameter controls how often a new random line is selected
from the loaded content (in seconds).

An interval of 0 will make it pick a line only once per session.

For local files, just replace '<file_name.txt>' with your file path.
Local files HAVE to be placed in FancyMenu's ASSETS folder!

languages.English:
The layout index is useful when you have
multiple layouts active for the same screen.
If these layouts need to get loaded
in a specific order, use the layout index.
The bigger the index, the later the layout
gets loaded, which means it is ON TOP OF
layouts with a smaller index.

For example: A layout with index 1 will
be under a layout with index 2.

languages.English:
Select a shader source file from local storage, a web URL, or a resource location.
The file must contain plain text GLSL fragment shader code (not binary).
Accepted entry points:
- Shadertoy style: void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord)
- Direct fragment style: void main()
In direct mode, output should be written to an out vec4 variable (recommended) or gl_FragColor compatibility.
Supported local file extension: .txt only.
Important: extension is only used for filtering; the content must still be fragment shader code.

The maximum number of client ticks to wait for the server to send the content of the player inventory. 
If locked slots get items moved out/thrown away on dimension change you need to increase this value.
This often happens on servers under heavy load.
NOTE: 20 ticks are equivalent of 1 second.
§l§cWARNING§r: Setting this too high MAY lead to locked slot management not working properly until this timeout expires.

- §z$$block_pos_x §r= The X coordinate of the targeted block

- §z$$block_pos_z §r= The Z coordinate of the targeted block
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the block hit position

in a different way than normal.

This mode makes the element always keep the exact same distance
to its anchor, no matter the current size of the element.

without it moving away or getting closer to its anchor.
While this can be useful in some situations, there
are also cases where this behaviour is not optimal.

languages.English:
This listener triggers once whenever the weather state changes (clear, rain, or thunder).
It will also re-trigger when the local weather changes, which means if it is raining, for example, and you enter a biome that has no rain (desert) or a biome where it is snowing, the listener will re-trigger even though the global weather didn't change.
Entering a building also counts as local weather change while it is raining outside, because well, it doesn't rain inside.

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$weather_type §r= The new global weather type (clear, rain, thunder)
- §z$$weather_can_snow §r= TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as snow
- §z$$weather_can_rain §r= TRUE when precipitation at the player renders as rain

It provides the following variables for its actions and requirements:

- §z$$entity_key §r= The resource location of the targeted entity type
- §z$$distance_to_player §r= The distance from the player's eyes to the entity hit position

- §z$$entity_pos_y §r= The entity's Y coordinate
- §z$$entity_pos_z §r= The entity's Z coordinate
- §z$$entity_uuid §r= The UUID of the targeted entity

languages.English:
All versions. **A key optimization.** Newer Minecraft versions (after 1.12) implemented a blockstate cache system that caches frequently used information about a blockstate, such as whether it is solid, its collision shape, etc. Rebuilding this cache is quite fast in vanilla (it takes only a second or two) but is quite slow with many mods installed, as there are many more blockstates present in the game which all must have their caches rebuilt.

This problem is exacerbated by Forge as the cache is rebuilt at many points when the data would almost certainly be unused before the next rebuild. Examples include right before reaching the main menu (during the "Freezing data" stage), as well as multiple (!) times when a world is being loaded.

ModernFix solves this performance bottleneck by instead making cache rebuilds lazy. Each blockstate rebuilds its cache the first time the data would be accessed. At any point when vanilla or Forge would attempt to rebuild caches for all blockstates, this is redirected to simply invalidate the cache on each blockstate instead.

This should not have any impact on TPS after startup concludes.

languages.English:
All versions. **A key optimization.** Launches on modern versions are heavily bottlenecked by filesystem access. Many requests are frequently made to resource packs to list resources or check if a given resource exists, and each of these result in a very slow file API call.

ModernFix completely eliminates most of the bottleneck here by simply caching a listing of all resources that exist within mod-provided and vanilla resourcepacks. The cache is rebuilt on resource reload (except for the vanilla resources, since they should never change while the game is running).

There are no known compatibility issues with this patch except for OptiFine (its CTM resources do not load correctly). However I do not recommend using OptiFine in any scenario, as it adds several minutes to launch time by itself and is not tested with ModernFix at all.

languages.English:
Check if the current GUI scale is X.

You can check for bigger than ('>'),
smaller than ('<') and equals X.

For example, if you want to check
if the scale is smaller than 3.20,
type '<3.20' (without the '').
To check if the scale is equal to 1.0,
just type '1.0' (without the '').
When checking if the scale is bigger than 2.20,
type '>2.20' (without the '').

Separate multiple conditions with commas.
Equality values are alternatives, while all
'>' and '<' conditions must be met.
